name: Baby Blue Eyes
lede: Baby Blue Eyes is a pale, soft blue listed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955, sharing its name with a California wildflower.

sections.title: A name in the library
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 lists this hue in block 180, among the very light blues [1]. Wikipedia's entry on the color cites the earlier Plochere system as its source, though no date survives in the library record for that citation [1]. The name is shared with *Nemophila menziesii*, a low, blue-flowered annual commonly called baby blue eyes, though no source here confirms this color name was drawn directly from the flower [4].

The nearest color-graph neighbor is [[pale-cerulean]], 3.2 units away, with the basic term [[sky]] and [[light-grey-blue]] close behind, and [[light-cornflower-blue]] and [[uranian-blue]] a touch further; [[aero]], a separate library entry, sits 9.6 units off [2]. Munsell gives 3.3PB 7.9/6.1, a light, moderately pale blue [1]. The hex #A1CAF1 is a screen approximation of the dictionary swatch [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale blue in 22 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.09 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest dated match is Filippino Lippi's *The Meeting of Joachim and Anne outside the Golden Gate of Jerusalem* (1497), a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. Later strong matches include Johan Jongkind's *Vue de Paris, la Seine, l'Estacade* (1853) and Piet Mondrian's early, representational *Polder Landscape with a Train and a Small Windmill on the Horizon* (1906), decades before his abstract grids [3]. Swedish and Danish paintings both show it well above the archive's average rate [3]. This is a computed color match, not a pigment test, on photographed, varnished canvases [3].
